However this is degraded UX/backgound-work waste for an edge case, not clearly a correctness defect — the reload loop may eventually succeed when retrieval succeeds, and there is no incorrect output, so it's a substantive design concern (missing failure handling for newly added logic) rather than a confirmed bug.

judged_text: The loading page reloads every 30 seconds unconditionally, with no terminal state for the case where retrieval never succeeds. For an embed_url whose article cannot be fetched (404, timeout, non-HTML page), a visitor's browser loops forever: each reload finds no topic and enqueues another RetrieveTopic job (throttled to one per 60 seconds per URL), so the page never shows content or an error and keeps generating background work indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, the page always calls `document.location.reload()` after 30 seconds with no success/failure terminal state. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, it unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`. Therefore, if retrieval never succeeds (e.g., remote fetch fails), each reload will keep rendering `loading` and enqueueing another `RetrieveTopic` job. Although `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` throttles the *work* to at most once per 60s per URL, the repeated reload + enqueue loop is still infinite and keeps generating background jobs indefinitely.
